source_lineage.excerpt:
Q. I have installed the Subscription and when I attempt to login all I get is a big white screen. How do I get my subscription started?
A. The most likely cause of this issue is installation of the 32bit IBM SPSS Statistics Subscription software on a 64bit machine. To fix the issue, please uninstall the 32bit and download and install the 64bit application from your Products & Services window on IBM.com. If you find that this does not resolve your issue, you have a new issue. Please open a Service Request using the Client Support Portal: http://ibm.biz/IBMClientSuccessPortal [http://ibm.biz/IBMClientSuccessPortal].

IBM SPSS Statistics Trial FAQ

Q. I have downloaded and installed Statistics Trial. When I start the product I get a big white box and then nothing else happens. How can I resolve this?
A. This issue is specific to Windows and is most likely caused by installing the 32-bit version of Statistics on a 64-bit machine. To correct the problem, please uninstall the 32-bit, and download an install the 64 bit version of Statistics. 

Q. I have downloaded and installed the Statistics Trial, but when I attempt to start I receive the message: 

 * 
 * https://spsslicensing.mybluemix.net
 *

Q. I attempted to register with my IBM ID, however a timeout message was received. 
A. This is likely related to a network/website issue. Exit Modeler, clear your browser cache, re-launch then continue with the login/create your IBM ID process. 


Q: Error 7001 when starting IBM SPSS Trial of Modeler. 
>Error # 7001 
>There is no license for IBM SPSS Modeler. This could be due to a missing 
>license file or no more network licenses available. For detailed information 
>about this problem, run the 'showlic' utility found in the product 
>installation directory. 
>Execution of this command stops. 

A: If you encountered an error 7001, with a message referring to a missing license file, it is likely that you installed by executing the ModelerClient64.msi, and not the Setup.exe file from the zip you downloaded. The .msi file is used only for silent or push installs of SPSS products. To correct the problem, you should uninstall the product, and then reinstall, but ensuring to run the Setup.exe file. We will be making improvements to rectify this issue. 

Q. I can’t start the trial. I get the following message: Error #2085. The temporary period for running IBM SPSS Modeler without a license has expired. Use the License Authorization Wizard to contact SPSS for a license code. Execution of this command stops. Specific symptom number: 37 
A. One or more of the following reasons may apply: 
1. Your 30 day trial period has expired for your installation. 
2. You may not have write permission to the lservrc file located in the SPSS Modeler bin directory. 
Please log in as a local Administrator and repeat the licensing process. 
3. An incorrect system date can sometimes cause this error message to occur. Check the system date/time on your machine and if it is incorrect, please reset to the current date and try running IBM SPSS Modeler again. 
4. The lservrc file may have two or more references to the IBM SPSS Modeler base module. You may want to delete the line that refers to the earliest expiration date, save the lservrc file, and run IBM SPSS Modeler. We have found instances where IBM SPSS Modeler reads the first license for the base module, and if the expiration date for that base module has passed, IBM SPSS Modeler will return Error 2085.

To correct this issue, configure your internet security program/firewall to allow access to the following URLs:

https://spsslicening.mybluemix.net
https://spsssub.ibm.com/licsrv

Also allow access to the following executable files:

spssengine.exe
jxbrowser-chromium.exe
stats.exe
java.exe
javaw.exe

When the installation finished you can use the launch button to start the Subscription edition: 

[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22004506&aid=8] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22004506&aid=8] 

After the program launched you can use the menu Help – Check for Updates to verify if there is no further update to install.

- DELETE the 2 folders spss250 and spssstatistics from this
   location.
   
   - Launch SPSS Subscription and click on Extensions - R 3.3
   configuration dialog
   - Define R home again with the path C:\Program Files\R\R-3.3.3.
   This will clean the installation of R plug in.
   
   - On output you should get:
   STATS R33 CONFIGURATION R_HOME="C:\Program Files\R\R-3.3.3".
   
   - Next, open a new syntax file and run:
   begin program R.
   print ("hello")
   end program.
   
   On Output you then should no longer get the error and the below
   text indicates that it works now:
   [1] "hello"
   
   Please note however that after that the folders are again
   installed to spss250 and spssstatistics
   C:\Users\<USERNAME>\Documents\R\win-library\3.3
   but with this workaround R will work with Subscription.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Smart Viewer comes automatically when installing SPSS. It is the SPSS output interface. It's on the program CD separately in case only Smart Viewer is wanted to be installed. It would require a separate license code

A: If you encountered an error 7001, with a message referring to a missing license file, it is likely that you installed by executing the ModelerClient64.msi, and not the Setup.exe file from the zip you downloaded. The .msi file is used only for silent or push installs of SPSS products. To correct the problem, you should uninstall the product, and then reinstall, but ensuring to run the Setup.exe file. We will be making improvements to rectify this issue. 

Q. I can’t start the trial. I get the following message: Error #2085. The temporary period for running IBM SPSS Modeler without a license has expired. Use the License Authorization Wizard to contact SPSS for a license code. Execution of this command stops. Specific symptom number: 37 
A. One or more of the following reasons may apply: 
1. Your 30 day trial period has expired for your installation. 
2. You may not have write permission to the lservrc file located in the SPSS Modeler bin directory. 
Please log in as a local Administrator and repeat the licensing process. 
3. An incorrect system date can sometimes cause this error message to occur. Check the system date/time on your machine and if it is incorrect, please reset to the current date and try running IBM SPSS Modeler again. 
4. The lservrc file may have two or more references to the IBM SPSS Modeler base module. You may want to delete the line that refers to the earliest expiration date, save the lservrc file, and run IBM SPSS Modeler. We have found instances where IBM SPSS Modeler reads the first license for the base module, and if the expiration date for that base module has passed, IBM SPSS Modeler will return Error 2085.
